exercises.instruction: Complete the sentences using might + a verb from the box:

parts: Don’t make too much noise. You
Be careful with your coffee. You
It’s better if we don’t talk so loud. Somebody
Be careful. This footpath is icy. You

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentences. Use might be able to or might have to + one of these verbs:

parts: I can come to the meeting, but I
I’m not free this evening, but I
I’m not sure whether this car park is free or not. We
‘I’ve got a problem with my bike.’ ‘Let me have a look. I

items.prompt: I haven’t seen him for a long time. I don’t know if I will recognise him or not.
We want to go to the game, but I don’t know whether we’ll be able to get tickets.
answers: We might not be able to get tickets for the game.

items.prompt: I said I’d do the shopping, but it’s possible I won’t have time.
answers: I might not have time to do the shopping.

items.prompt: I’ve been invited to the wedding, but I’m not sure that I’ll be able to go.
answers: I might not be able to go to the wedding.

exercises.instruction: Read the situations and write sentences with might as well.

items.prompt: Your computer doesn’t work any more. It will cost a lot to repair.
answers: I might as well buy a new one.

items.prompt: You’ve painted the kitchen. You still have a lot of paint, so why not paint the bathroom too?
answers: I might as well paint the bathroom too.

items.prompt: You and a friend are at home. You’re bored. There’s a film on TV starting in a few minutes.
answers: We might as well watch it.
